exercises.question: Which sentence uses a figurative gerund naturally to show attitude alongside the main action?
options: Respondió esquivando la pregunta con una sonrisa diplomática.
Respondió esquivó la pregunta con una sonrisa diplomática.
Respondió esquivado la pregunta con una sonrisa diplomática.
Respondió esquivar la pregunta con una sonrisa diplomática.

exercises.sentence: Escuchó la broma _____ calma, aunque estaba sorprendido.
exercises.english: He listened to the joke feigning calm, although he was surprised.

exercises.sentence: Aunque el debate se alargó, nadie quiso tirar la _____ antes del cierre.
exercises.english: Although the debate dragged on, nobody wanted to throw in the towel before the end.

exercises.sentence: La dueña siguió la tertulia haciendo la vista gorda ante el retraso, pero nadie quiso tirar la toalla con el capítulo.
options: The owner continued the reading circle turning a blind eye to the delay, and nobody wanted to give up on the chapter.
The owner stopped the reading circle turning a blind eye to the delay, and nobody wanted to give up on the chapter.
The owner continued the reading circle turning a blind eye to the delay, and everyone wanted to give up on the chapter.
The owner continued the reading circle complaining about the delay, and nobody wanted to give up on the chapter.

exercises.question: In the story, what did the bookshop owner propose at the start to break the ice?
options: That each person open a borrowed novel and comment on the first marked sentence they found.
That each person write an anonymous note about chapter four on a cardboard bookmark.
That Carlos and Meg read the opening page of the blue book aloud together.
That everyone share their favourite proverb from memory before drinking tea.

exercises.question: What detail allowed Meg to realise who had written the message on the bookmark?
options: The slanted handwriting was identical to the discount signs hanging by the till.
The cardboard matched the menus on the tables of the café.
The older man in the corner pointed directly at the bookshop owner.
The message quoted a phrase the owner had just used while serving tea.

exercises.question: How did Carlos and Meg view the trick differently by the end of the afternoon?
options: Carlos admitted he fell for the trap at first, while Meg said it broke the group's shyness and kept the thread going.
Carlos thought the trick was funny from the start, while Meg felt it had tangled the debate.
Both agreed the trick was a mistake that made readers lose the thread of chapter four.
Meg suspected the older man was behind it, while Carlos blamed the bookshop owner immediately.

prompt.speaker: Carlos
prompt.text: ¿Por qué no dijiste directamente quién había dejado el marcapáginas?

options: Preferí hablar insinuando la pista poco a poco y fingiendo duda.
Preferí hablar insinuaba la pista poco a poco y fingía duda.
Preferí hablar insinuado la pista poco a poco y fingido duda.
Preferí hablar a insinuar la pista poco a poco y de fingir duda.

template.prompt: Write one sentence using «haciendo la vista gorda» to say the owner continued the reading circle («La dueña siguió la tertulia») while turning a blind eye to the delay («ante el retraso»).
template.answer: La dueña siguió la tertulia haciendo la vista gorda ante el retraso.

exercises.question: Which sentence avoids the *gerundio de posterioridad* and expresses two sequential events cleanly?
options: Abrió la novela prestada y una hora después descubrió un marcapáginas escrito a mano.
Abrió la novela prestada, descubriendo una hora después un marcapáginas escrito a mano.
Abrió la novela prestada, devolviendo el libro la semana siguiente.
Abrió la novela prestada, terminando la tertulia dos horas más tarde.
